description: Universal rendering rules for image-to-3D conversion - includes visual presentation, 3D-safe geometry, and mesh reconstruction constraints

prop_visibility_modes.description: Defines how props interact with the character silhouette based on usage context

modes.presented: Prop held/displayed away from body; fully visible base-to-tip; clear negative space except at grip
modes.carried_attached: Prop worn/slung/holstered; overlap allowed at attachment zones; attachment method must be visible; item remains readable but does NOT require full base-to-tip visibility

generic_render_rules.description: Universal rendering rules for image-to-3D conversion
rules: SINGLE SUBJECT ONLY: exactly one character/creature in the entire image. NO other figures, NO background characters, NO companions, NO additional people or animals. Only the main subject.
FIGURE-ONLY PRESENTATION: background blank/featureless (no scenery, terrain, set dressing, environmental objects, diorama elements, bases, pedestals, plinths, stands, or ground plane).

Design-intent anchor (CRITICAL): conceptual sculpt design visualization intended for tabletop-scale physical reproduction; illustrative art direction, not real-world documentation or evidence; do not reference existing brands or manufactured products.
Prop constraint (CRITICAL): do not add props unless explicitly specified. Only include items clearly named and described. Do not invent extra weapons, holsters, pouches, talismans, or implements.
Image-to-3D optimization: all geometry designed for clean mesh reconstruction from single-view image input
Silhouette clarity: separate elements should have clear negative space separation unless overlapping for expressive pose with unambiguous depth order
Silhouette cleanliness prioritized over motion exaggeration
Do NOT invent additional cloth elements to imply motion

GEAR LOGIC PRIORITY: All equipment must read as functional, removable gear. Carried items must show attachment logic (straps, holsters, harnesses). Do NOT reinterpret gear as armor or decorative anatomy. Functional readability takes priority over silhouette cleanliness.
Depth disambiguation: overlapping elements allowed ONLY when depth order is unambiguous (one clearly in front/behind)
Contact minimization: minimize contact points between separate geometry when possible; expressive pose takes priority over maximum separation
Thickness enforcement: all features thick enough to read as geometry, not surface detail; minimum thickness equivalent to finger width at miniature scale
Edge simplification: hard edges preferred over soft transitions; clean plane breaks over gradual curves
Cavity avoidance: avoid deep recesses, sharp undercuts, and complex cavities that create reconstruction ambiguity
Element separation: each major element (body, cloth, props, limbs) must remain geometrically distinct volumes even when overlapping

material_appearance.title: MATERIAL & APPEARANCE
material_appearance.content:
Unpainted tabletop miniature sculpt.
Uniform matte mid-grey only.
No color variation, no textures.
Depth indicated ONLY by geometry.
Dark values represent DEPTH ONLY (recesses, undercuts, shadows) NOT color.
Surface color differences (e.g., eye pupils, dark fabric) rendered as mid-grey same as surrounding surfaces; only depth changes create value shifts.
Hard edges, simplified planes, medium-scale detail.
All small details chunky and readable at 28-32mm miniature scale.
No thin edges—every strap, trim, or edge as thick as a finger.
No micro-detail, no filigree, no surface noise.

geometry_constraints.title: 3D-SAFE GEOMETRY
geometry_constraints.content:
INTENTIONAL OVERLAP ENABLED:
Crossed arms, braced weapons, and controlled limb overlap are allowed when required for character expression, provided print-safe geometry is maintained.

WIELDED/HELD OBJECTS (in-hand items):
Angled in screen space (30-45 degrees)—NOT parallel to camera or torso.
Controlled contact or overlap with forearm, shoulder, or chest allowed if pose requires it; expressive pose takes priority over maximum separation.
Overlapping forms must remain distinct volumes with printable clearance (2–4mm equivalent).
Hands touch objects only at clear grip points.
Small held props thickened and rotated outward from body.

HOLSTERED/STOWED OBJECTS (not in-hand):
May be parallel to body or follow body contours.
Contact with belt, hip, thigh, or back attachment points is expected and acceptable.
Partial occlusion by clothing/body is acceptable as long as attachment method is visible.
Item must be distinct as a shape, but may NOT be distinct as a separate silhouette.
Holstered/sheathed items may not have visible clearance around the blade/barrel portion—only the exposed grip/handle may protrude.
Holstered shields: convex (domed) face outward; straps toward the body worn like a backpack; mounted center-back on the spine, symmetrically positioned.

GENERAL:
Cloth flows in one clear direction (behind/beside figure).
Cloth may approach but must not intersect or fuse with arms or wielded weapons.
Visible air gaps preferred between wielded elements unless pose intent requires overlap.
NO straps, slings, ropes, cords, thin dangling elements, or overlapping cloth.

facial_geometry.title: FACE (3D-SAFE)
facial_geometry.content:
Simplified sculptural forms, not deep anatomical detail.
Avoid deep sockets, sharp undercuts, complex cavities.
Brow as subtle raised plane; eyes as simple almond forms with visible lids.
Nose as subtle raised form with soft transitions.
Mouth open or closed for expression; if open, moderate depth (2-3mm equivalent) with simplified interior.
Fangs as simplified projecting tooth forms.
Expression through mouth shape and head angle.
Facial planes must remain broad and under-resolved; no edge sharpening, no thin bevels, no small curvature transitions within facial features.
Facial surfaces intentionally left slightly blocky and faceted at tabletop scale to preserve printability.

pose_constraints.title: POSE CLARITY
pose_constraints.content:
One pose only, one emotional state only.
Each limb has one clear job (grip, gesture, support, or rest).
No mixed or transitional poses.

framing.title: FRAMING
framing.content:
Single humanoid figure, full body visible head-to-feet, centered.
Neutral blank background.
Full-body figure entirely visible from head to feet; no cropping at ankles, knees, hips, shoulders, elbows, wrists, or head.
All limbs fully inside frame; no cinematic crop, no hero crop, no portrait crop.
Generous negative space around entire figure.
View: 3/4 (~45 degree rotation)—three-quarter sculpt view, NOT straight-on front view.
Orthographic or near-orthographic projection for accurate geometry.
Camera pulled back to include entire silhouette.
No close-up, no medium shot, no waist-up framing.
Framing priority over facial detail.
No cinematic perspective.

rendering.title: RENDERING
rendering.content:
Photographed unpainted resin sculpt.
Product photography lighting: diffuse neutral illumination with soft overhead key light.
Clean readable forms with natural value transitions from depth and geometry.
Matte resin surface; no specular highlights; no glossy reflections.
Depth expressed through natural shadowing in recesses and under raised forms.
Form separation through geometry, not dramatic lighting contrast.
Avoid illustrative or graphic rendering: no posterized values, no hard shadow lines, no graphic edge emphasis.
Natural soft shadows where forms meet; avoid artificial contrast jumps.
Even, controlled lighting—NO dramatic directional lighting, NO rim lighting effects, NO cinematic lighting.
Avoid fine microtexture, micro-noise, realistic skin pores, strand-level detail.
No lens effects (flare, bokeh), no film grain, no subsurface scattering, no volumetric glow, no chromatic aberration.
Clean product documentation aesthetic; neutral background; professional studio setup.
